# hfy

> hfy is a self-hosted backend and embeddable chat UI for AI conversations: one Go binary plus Postgres (with pgvector), configured by one YAML file. The host app keeps its users and data. It creates conversations and short-lived access grants over HTTP. hfy runs the agent loop, calls tools from MCP servers, stores every step as an append-only event, streams the reply over SSE and serves a ready-made chat UI at `/embed` for iframes and mobile WebViews.

This file is the complete integration guide for AI coding agents. It is self-contained, so you should not need any other page to integrate hfy into an app. Source: https://github.com/alash3al/hfy. Full human reference: https://github.com/alash3al/hfy/blob/main/docs/reference.md (canonical if anything here disagrees).

## How to use this guide

To add an AI chat to an existing app, follow "Integration recipe" in order. Use "Reference" for exact shapes. Check "Rules" before you finish, and use "Troubleshooting" when something fails.

Choose the client surface first:

1. **Embedded UI (default, recommended).** iframe on the web, WebView in mobile apps. No UI code; the host only supplies grants.
2. **JS client (`/embed/client.js`).** For a fully custom web UI. A DOM-free class that handles history, streaming, reconnects, token refresh, uploads and approvals.
3. **Raw HTTP + SSE.** Native mobile UIs, or other languages.

## Concepts

- **Instance.** One hfy deployment serves one app (one tenant). Many end users share it; isolation is per conversation. Run another instance for another app.
- **Conversation.** A room, created by the host backend. Holds the full, never-deleted event history. Several people and several agents may share one.
- **Grant.** Access for one person (an `actor`) to one conversation. The backend creates it with the server secret and gets a token `hfy_…` (default lifetime 1 h, max 24 h). The client uses only that token. Tokens are never cookies.
- **Actor.** The host's own user id for the person (max 256 bytes). It is recorded on their messages and shown to the model and to other participants.
- **Agent.** A configured assistant: model, system prompt, tools, limits. `agent:` is the default agent `main`; `agents:` adds named ones. The grant picks which agent answers that person.
- **Turn.** One user message and everything the agent does in response. Turns run one at a time per conversation; later messages queue.
- **Event.** Every step (message, tool call, tool result, state change, approval) is an append-only event. History and the live stream use the same envelope.
- **Tools.** All external tools come from MCP servers (local stdio commands or remote Streamable HTTP). hfy also ships core built-ins: `hfy.now`, `hfy.math_calc`, `hfy.tool_search`, `hfy.conversation_search` (with embeddings), opt-in `hfy.ask_user`, and sub-agents as `hfy.<name>`.
- **Server secret.** `server.secret` (usually `${HFY_SERVER_SECRET}`). Backend-only. Backend routes never answer browsers (no CORS), so it cannot work from a page.

## Integration recipe

### 1. Run hfy

Requirements: Postgres with pgvector 0.8.0+, and an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, …). For a first run without any model, use the built-in `mock` provider (see Config).

Prebuilt binary (Linux, macOS, Windows; amd64 and arm64), from the latest GitHub release:

```sh
# pick one: linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_amd64, darwin_arm64 (.tar.gz); windows_amd64, windows_arm64 (.zip)
curl -sSL https://github.com/alash3al/hfy/releases/latest/download/hfy_linux_amd64.tar.gz | tar xz
./hfy_linux_amd64/hfy version
```

Docker image: `ghcr.io/alash3al/hfy` (tags `latest`, `1`, `1.0`, `1.0.0`; linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). Config is read from `/etc/hfy/hfy.yaml`; the default command is `serve --work` on port 8080.

Docker Compose (from a clone of the repo; starts hfy and Postgres together):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/alash3al/hfy && cd hfy
export HFY_SERVER_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
docker compose run --rm --no-deps hfy config:example > hfy.yaml   # commented starter config
# edit hfy.yaml (provider, model, context_window, system prompt, cors_origins)
docker compose up        # API + workers on :8080; migrations run on boot
```

Inside Docker, `localhost` is the container. To reach Ollama on the host, use `http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1` (add `extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` to the service on Linux).

Binary (prebuilt as above, or `go install github.com/alash3al/hfy@latest`):

```sh
hfy config:example > hfy.yaml
export HFY_SERVER_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:hfy@localhost:5432/hfy
hfy -c hfy.yaml validate          # checks config, env expansion, startup rules
hfy -c hfy.yaml serve --work      # API + workers in one process
```

Commands: `serve [--work]`, `queue:work [-q turns,embeddings] [--workers N]` (workers only, scale separately), `validate`, `migrate [up|down|status]`, `config:example`, `version`. `-c` may also come from `HFY_CONFIG`.

Health: `GET /healthz` (process alive), `GET /readyz` (Postgres reachable, else 503).

### 2. Minimal config

```yaml
server:
  secret: ${HFY_SERVER_SECRET}
  cors_origins: ["https://app.example.com"]   # every origin that iframes /embed or calls client routes from a browser

database:
  url: ${DATABASE_URL}

providers:
  openai:
    url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}
    timeout: 60s

agent:
  model: openai/gpt-4o-mini          # <provider name>/<model id>
  settings: { temperature: 0.2, context_window: 128000 }   # context_window is REQUIRED
  system: |
    You are the support assistant for {{company}}. You are talking to {{user_name}}.
  vars:
    company:   { default: "Acme" }
    user_name: { required: true }
  ask_user: true                     # optional: lets the agent ask structured questions
```

No model yet? Use the mock provider. It streams a fixed reply in-process, so the whole stack (UI included) runs without a model server:

```yaml
providers:
  mock:
    type: mock
    mock: { reply: "Hello from mock", embed_dimensions: 768 }
agent:
  model: mock/demo
  settings: { context_window: 8192 }
```

### 3. Backend: create conversations and grants

All backend calls use `Authorization: Bearer <server.secret>` and JSON bodies.

```http
POST /v1/conversations
→ 201 {"id": "<conversation uuid>"}

POST /v1/grants
{"conversation": "<uuid>", "actor": "user-42", "agent": "main", "vars": {"user_name": "Sara"}, "expires_in": 3600}
→ 201 {"id": "<grant uuid>", "token": "hfy_…", "expires_at": "<RFC3339>"}

DELETE /v1/grants/{id}   → 204 (revoke now; open streams end within 15 s)
```

Persist the conversation id in your own database (for example one per user, per support ticket or per order), and create it once. Create a fresh grant every time the widget asks for one, and only after your normal session/auth check. Never cache or reuse tokens across users. The token is returned once (hfy stores only its SHA-256).

Grant fields:
- `conversation` (required), `actor` (required, your user id).
- `agent`: which configured agent answers this person (`main` default, or a key under `agents:`).
- `vars`: values for the agent's declared `{{vars}}`, rendered into the system prompt. A var that is undeclared, or required but missing, is a 400. Backend-only, so the client can never set them. Every MCP server receives them in `_meta`, so never put secrets in vars.
- `scope`: whose memory `hfy.conversation_search` searches (default: the actor).
- `expires_in`: seconds, default 3600, max 86400.

Example backend endpoint (Node/Express; translate to the app's stack):

```js
const HFY = process.env.HFY_URL;                       // e.g. https://hfy.example.com
const auth = { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.HFY_SERVER_SECRET}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" };

app.post("/api/chat/grant", requireLogin, async (req, res) => {
  let conversation = await db.getChatConversation(req.user.id);
  if (!conversation) {
    const r = await fetch(`${HFY}/v1/conversations`, { method: "POST", headers: auth });
    if (!r.ok) return res.status(502).end();
    conversation = (await r.json()).id;
    await db.saveChatConversation(req.user.id, conversation);
  }
  const g = await fetch(`${HFY}/v1/grants`, {
    method: "POST", headers: auth,
    body: JSON.stringify({ conversation, actor: String(req.user.id), vars: { user_name: req.user.firstName } }),
  });
  if (!g.ok) return res.status(502).end();
  const { token, expires_at } = await g.json();
  res.json({ token, expires_at });                    // never return the server secret
});
```

### 4. Web: embed the chat in an iframe

The host page's origin must be listed in `server.cors_origins`. That list is also the iframe's CSP `frame-ancestors`; without it, the browser refuses to frame `/embed`.

```html
<iframe id="hfy-chat" src="https://hfy.example.com/embed" title="Chat"
        style="border:0;width:100%;height:640px" allow="clipboard-write"></iframe>
<script>
  const HFY_ORIGIN = "https://hfy.example.com";
  const frame = document.getElementById("hfy-chat");

  window.addEventListener("message", async (e) => {
    if (e.origin !== HFY_ORIGIN || e.source !== frame.contentWindow) return;
    let msg; try { msg = typeof e.data === "string" ? JSON.parse(e.data) : e.data; } catch { return; }

    if (msg.type === "ready") {
      // optional per-viewer presentation
      frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ v: 1, type: "configure", lang: document.documentElement.lang || "en", theme: "auto" }, HFY_ORIGIN);
    }
    if (msg.type === "token-needed") {             // msg.reason: "initial" | "expired" | "unauthorized"
      const r = await fetch("/api/chat/grant", { method: "POST", credentials: "same-origin" });
      if (!r.ok) return;                           // e.g. logged out: the widget keeps waiting
      const { token, expires_at } = await r.json();
      frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ v: 1, type: "grant", token, expires_at }, HFY_ORIGIN);
    }
  });
</script>
```

The widget keeps the token in memory only. It asks again (`token-needed`) on expiry or a 401, then resumes the stream from its last event without gaps or duplicates. There is no URL configuration: `/embed` is always a bare URL, and you must never put a token in its query string.

### 5. Mobile: embed the chat in a WebView

**Flutter apps: use the native hfy_flutter SDK (in development); do not embed /embed in a WebView.**

Load `https://<hfy>/embed` top-level in the WebView. Messages go out from the widget as a JSON string, and come back in by calling `window.hfy.receive(json)`. The widget picks the first outbound bridge that exists:

1. `window.HfyBridge.postMessage(str)`: Android `addJavascriptInterface(obj, "HfyBridge")` with a `@JavascriptInterface fun postMessage(s: String)`.
2. `window.webkit.messageHandlers.hfy.postMessage(str)`: iOS/macOS WKWebView, `userContentController.add(handler, name: "hfy")`.
3. `window.chrome.webview.postMessage(str)`: Windows WebView2.
4. `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(str)`: React Native `react-native-webview`, via `onMessage`.

Inbound, from any shell: evaluate `window.hfy.receive(<json string or object>)`.

React Native:

```jsx
<WebView ref={ref} source={{ uri: "https://hfy.example.com/embed" }}
  onMessage={async (e) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(e.nativeEvent.data);
    if (msg.type === "token-needed") {
      const g = await api.chatGrant();
      const out = JSON.stringify({ v: 1, type: "grant", token: g.token, expires_at: g.expires_at });
      ref.current.injectJavaScript(`window.hfy.receive(${JSON.stringify(out)}); true;`);
    }
  }} />
```

### 6. Presentation

Defaults live in YAML under `embed:` and are validated at startup:

```yaml
embed:
  lang: en              # omit = viewer's browser language
  dir: auto             # auto | ltr | rtl
  theme: auto           # light | dark | auto
  accent: "#0b7d71"     # hex
  density: comfortable  # comfortable | compact
  layout: bubbles       # bubbles | transcript
  tool_calls: summary   # hidden | summary (friendly one-line rows) | details (args and results, for developers)
```

For per-viewer overrides, send a bridge message `{"v":1,"type":"configure", …}` with any of `lang`, `dir`, `theme`, `accent`, `density`, `layout`, `tool_calls`, and `strings` (an object overriding UI strings). Built-in strings are English and Arabic. Time zone, language and direction auto-detect from the viewer. Arbitrary CSS/HTML and trust fields (token, API base, actor, agent, vars) are never client-configurable.

What the UI does by itself: message bubbles with delivery ticks, streamed markdown, copy, photo/document attachments (when `filesystem:` is configured), approvals and `hfy.ask_user` questions as bottom sheets, tool cards (`_meta["hfy/ui"]`, see MCP section) with send/link/host buttons, Send turns into Stop while the viewer's own turn runs, history paging, reconnects, multi-viewer rooms, dark mode, RTL.

### 7. Give the agent tools (MCP)

```yaml
mcp:
  orders:
    type: remote                                  # Streamable HTTP
    url: https://internal.example.com/mcp
    headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${ORDERS_MCP_TOKEN}" }
    approval: [refund, cancel_*]                  # these tools wait for the viewer's approval, for every agent
    approve_destructive: true                     # also wait on tools annotated destructiveHint: true
    ui:                                           # opt the server's tools into cards + tool-triggered questions
      image_hosts: ["img.shop.example", "*.imgshop.net"]  # https hosts allowed in cards' images
  files:
    type: local                                   # stdio command, started by hfy
    command: [mcp-filesystem, /data]
    environment: { LOG: "1" }                     # its only env besides PATH, HOME, USER, locale, TMPDIR, TZ
    timeout: 2m                                   # per tool call (default 2m)
agent:
  mcp: [orders]        # optional; omit = all servers, reached through hfy.tool_search (smaller prompt)
```

Every tool call carries `_meta["hfy/turn"] = {conversation, turn, call_id, agent, actor: {type, ref}, scope, vars}`. **Authorize inside the MCP server from `_meta.actor.ref`** (the person who started the turn); the model cannot change `_meta`. Return MCP `structuredContent` for data meant for client UIs; the model sees the text content. An opted-in tool result may ship a display card in `_meta["hfy/ui"]` (see "Tool cards" below) — v1.1.0 renamed these keys from the old `io.github.alash3al.hfy/*` spelling; servers must send `hfy/turn` and `hfy/ui`.

Knowledge / RAG: hfy has no document store. Expose your docs, catalog or help center as an MCP search tool (filtered by `_meta.actor`), and the agent calls it when needed. For small, fixed knowledge, put it in the system prompt or pass it via grant `vars`.

## Reference

### Config sections

`server`, `database`, `providers`, `mcp`, `agent` (required except `mcp`), plus optional `agents`, `subagents`, `queue`, `retention`, `embeddings`, `attachments`, `filesystem`, `summarizer`, `metrics`, `embed`.

- `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` expand in string values (never keys). A missing variable without a default stops startup and names it. `$$` is a literal `$`. Quote inside YAML flow maps: `{ a: "${X}" }`.
- Unknown keys stop startup with their line number.
- `providers.<name>`: `url`, `api_key`, `timeout` (longest silence while streaming), `type: openai` (default) or `mock`.
- `agent` / `agents.<name>`: `model` (`<provider>/<model>`), `settings` (`temperature`, `context_window` required, `vision`: accept image attachments, default false), `system` (supports `{{vars}}`), `vars` (`{default: …}` or `{required: true}`), `limits` (`steps`, `total_tokens`, `timeout` per turn), `approval` (`tools`: `<server>.<tool>` patterns, `timeout`), `ask_user` (bool), `mcp` (list of server names).
- `subagents.<name>`: `description`, `model`, `system`, `mcp`, `limits`. Every agent may call them as tool `hfy.<name>`. They are isolated (they get only the task text), depth 1, and their usage counts toward the parent turn.
- `embeddings`: `{model: <provider>/<model>, dimensions: N}`. Enables `hfy.conversation_search` over earlier messages of the same `scope`.
- `summarizer`: `{model, settings, keep_recent, system?}`. History is summarized when the next prompt would pass 80% of `context_window`. Nothing is deleted.
- `attachments`: `{allowed_hosts, types, max_bytes, max_count}` for attachments hosted by your app (by URL).
- `filesystem`: `{dsn: "s3://bucket?region=…" | "file:///path", public_url, types, max_bytes (10MB), upload_ttl (5m), download_ttl (15m)}` enables uploads through hfy. `file://` needs `public_url`. S3 needs bucket CORS allowing PUT from embed origins.
- `queue`: `{workers: 4, lease: 30s, max_attempts: 3}`. `retention`: `{trace: 30d}`. `metrics`: `{listen: "127.0.0.1:9090"}` (Prometheus `/metrics` plus health, on a separate port).

`hfy config:example` prints the full commented reference.

### Client HTTP API

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <grant token>` (on `/events` also `?token=` for `EventSource`). The grant names the conversation, so paths name none.

- `POST /v1/conversation/messages` `{text, attachments?}` → `202 {"turn": uuid}`. Starts a turn or queues it behind the active one.
  - Attachment: `{url, mime, name?}` (host-hosted, checked against `attachments:`) or `{file, mime, name?}` (an upload slot key).
- `POST /v1/conversation/uploads` `{mime, size}` → `{file, upload_url, expires_at, direct}`. PUT the bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: <mime>`: if `direct` is true it is a presigned S3 URL (no auth header); otherwise it is an hfy path, so prefix the hfy base URL and send the grant `Authorization`. Then post a message with `{file, mime}`.
- `GET /v1/conversation/events` SSE. `id` = event uuid, `event` = type, `data` = envelope. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`, or `?after=<event uuid>`. Without either it starts from now. `: ping` every 15 s. The stream ends when the grant ends.
- `GET /v1/conversation/history?limit=&before=` → durable events grouped by turn, newest page first; `next` (older-page cursor), `live_after` (open `/events?after=<live_after>` to continue without a gap), `viewer` (this grant's actor, to recognize own messages).
- `POST /v1/conversation/approvals` `{call_id, approve, result?, answers?}`. Only the actor who started the turn decides (else 403). For `hfy.ask_user` — or a tool call that asked questions of its own — approve with `answers: {"<question id>": value}`, validated against the stored questions (400 names the bad one). Decline with `approve: false`; `answers` on a plain approval are a 400.
- `POST /v1/conversation/stop` stops the caller's own active turn and their queued ones.

Errors are `{"error": "..."}`: 400 bad input, 401 missing/unknown/expired/revoked token, 403 not your turn or the grant's agent no longer exists, 404 unknown conversation or grant, 409 no pending approval, 413 body over 2 MiB.

The API is versioned in the path (`/v1`). Within v1, changes are additive only.

### Events

Envelope (stream and history):

```json
{"id":"…","type":"tool_call","parent":"<turn uuid>","actor":{"uuid":"…","type":"agent","ref":"main"},
 "v":1,"data":{"name":"orders.lookup","call_id":"c1","arguments":{}},"created_at":"…"}
```

Types: `turn` (root, `parent` null; `data.agent`) · `turn.state` (`queued` `running` `awaiting_approval` `completed` `failed` `stopped` `cancelled`) · `turn.cancel_requested` · `message.text` (`{text, attachments?}`) · `reasoning` · `tool_call` · `tool_call.interrupted` · `tool_result` (`content`, `is_error`, optional `structured`, optional `ui` — the sanitized `_meta["hfy/ui"]` card) · `approval.requested` (a tool's own questions add `questions`, `ui` and `held`) · `approval.decided` · `model.usage` · `summary` · ephemeral, live-only: `text.delta`, `reasoning.delta`.

Rendering rules: append `text.delta` under its turn, then replace it with the durable `message.text`. Pair `tool_call` and `tool_result` by `data.call_id`. Ignore unknown types. Served attachments for stored files carry a fresh signed `url`.

### JS client (custom web UI)

```html
<script src="https://hfy.example.com/embed/client.js"></script>
<script>
  const client = new HfyClient({
    api: "https://hfy.example.com",
    onTokenNeeded: async (reason) => (await fetch("/api/chat/grant", { method: "POST" })).json(), // → {token, expires_at}
  });
  client.onEvent((envelope) => render(envelope));   // history and live events, deduped
  client.onState((state) => showConnection(state));
  await client.connect();
  await client.send("hello");                        // also: upload(file) → attachment, approve(callId, approve, result, answers), stop(), loadOlder(), close()
</script>
```

The page's origin must be in `server.cors_origins`.

### hfy.ask_user

Enable it with `ask_user: true` on a top-level agent (not available to sub-agents). One call pauses the turn with 1–10 questions of type `single`/`multi` (2–20 options), `text` or `confirm`. The UI shows them as a step-by-step sheet. The model gets `{"answers": {...}}`, "The user declined to answer.", or "The user did not answer in time." (agent `approval.timeout`, else 30m). Small slips from small models (string options, odd ids, type synonyms) are repaired. Small models (around 3B) often ask in plain text instead of calling the tool; use a stronger model or say "ask with hfy.ask_user" in the system prompt.

### Tool cards (`_meta["hfy/ui"]`)

An MCP server can put a display card (or carousel) in a tool result's `_meta["hfy/ui"]`, and — when both the server (`mcp.<name>.ui` in hfy's config) and the agent (`ask_user: true`) allow — structured questions that attach to the tool's **own** call: the turn pauses on the real call, the viewer answers in the approval sheet, and the model receives the tool's text joined with `{"answers": {...}}`. hfy rebuilds the block server-side before any viewer sees it: unknown fields are dropped, strings clipped, urls filtered, limits enforced (32 KiB total, 6 kv rows, 3 buttons, 10 cards, payload ≤ 2 KiB). The model never sees the card. **Upgrade every hfy instance before any MCP server starts sending `hfy/ui`: an older binary never reads `_meta`, so the whole feature is inert there. And do not enable `ui:` in a running cluster gradually: an older worker resuming a held ask after the viewer's answer was recorded ignores the unknown fields on the stored `approval.requested` and re-executes the tool. Upgrade all instances and drain in-flight held asks before enabling `ui:` anywhere; strict config (unknown keys stop startup) only protects a fresh start.**

The block, sent as ordinary JSON under `_meta["hfy/ui"]`:

```json
{"v": 1, "type": "card", "title": "Your order", "subtitle": "Pizza Express", "body": "Margherita, extra cheese", "badge": "12 EUR",
 "kv": [{"label": "Size", "value": "Large"}, {"label": "Delivery", "value": "30–40 min"}],
 "image": "https://img.shop.example/margherita.jpg", "buttons": [
   {"send": {"label": "Order it"}},
   {"link": {"label": "Menu", "url": "https://shop.example/menu"}},
   {"host": {"label": "Pay now", "name": "pay_host", "payload": {"amount": 12}}}]}

{"type": "action", "v": 1, "name": "pay_host", "payload": {"amount": 12}, "call_id": "01JD..."}  // what the host receives when "Pay now" is clicked

{"v": 1, "type": "carousel", "cards": [
  {"v": 1, "type": "card", "title": "Margherita", "body": "12 EUR", "image": "https://img.shop.example/m.jpg"},
  {"v": 1, "type": "card", "title": "Capriciosa", "body": "14 EUR", "image": "https://img.shop.example/c.jpg"}]}
```

The `//` comments are doc-only. Questions never live on a button: they are a top-level field of the block, always shaped `{"questions": [...]}` like `hfy.ask_user`'s arguments:

```json
{"v": 1, "type": "card", "title": "Your order", "body": "Margherita, 12 EUR", "image": "https://img.shop.example/m.jpg",
 "buttons": [{"send": {"label": "Order it"}}],
 "questions": {"questions": [{"id": "size", "text": "Which size?", "type": "single", "options": [{"value": "s", "label": "Small"}, {"value": "l", "label": "Large"}]}]}}
```

A carousel is `{"v": 1, "type": "carousel", "cards": [<card>, ...]}` (up to 10). If the questions part is unusable the card survives; if the card part is unusable (no title and no body, bad carousel) only the questions survive — nothing renders, but the turn still pauses on their answers; a questions-only block (no card at all) is allowed too, same behavior. Wrong `v` drops the whole block. An ui-carrying tool that **also** needs approval cannot ask: approval pauses first, and after it the questions are dropped (log a warning). Stopping the turn while the questions are open ends it with the held tool result plus "The user stopped before answering.".

Host actions arrive as `{"v": 1, "type": "action", "name": "<name>", "payload": {...}, "call_id": "<call>"}` over the widget bridge (`window.HfyBridge.postMessage`, webkit messageHandlers, `chrome.webview`, ReactNativeWebView, or `postMessage` when framed); send the token the same way (`token-needed` / `hfy.receive`). Send buttons are live only on the viewer's own, current turn; link buttons always are.

Mobile hosts: Android WebView needs the file-chooser callback (`onShowFileChooser` → Activity result) wired for document/attachment picking; this is documented here, not device-tested.

### Approvals

The default is never to ask. A call waits for the viewer when it matches its server's `mcp.<name>.approval` patterns (tool names without the server prefix), or its server has `approve_destructive: true` and the tool is annotated destructive, or it matches the agent's `approval.tools` (`<server>.<tool>` globs). Agents can only add rules, never remove a server's. Core built-ins never ask, and naming one in `approval.tools` is a startup error. A pause blocks the conversation until the turn's starter decides or `approval.timeout` passes (rejected). Approvals cover an agent's own calls; to guard what a sub-agent can reach, guard `hfy.<subagent>`.

### Behavior you can rely on

- Crash safety: an expired worker lease re-runs the turn from its events. A tool call in flight when a worker died is never re-run; the model is told it was interrupted.
- Loop: tool errors and invalid arguments go back to the model as error results. The same call a third time is refused; a sixth ends the turn. Provider 429/5xx/network errors retry up to `queue.max_attempts`.
- Multi-party: every agent in a room sees the whole conversation. Others' messages are framed with who wrote them; frames are not authorization.
- Images go to the model only in the turn they arrive in, as URLs the provider must be able to fetch. Non-image files reach the model as their key only.
- Retention: ephemeral events, traces, finished jobs and ended grants expire after `retention.trace`; messages and usage are permanent.

## Rules

Do:
- Keep `HFY_SERVER_SECRET` on the server. Create conversations and grants only from the backend, after the app's own auth check.
- Store the conversation id per user/room in the app's database; create a new grant per widget request.
- Add every embedding origin (scheme + host + port, exactly as the browser sends it) to `server.cors_origins`.
- Set `context_window` to the model's real window, or somewhat below it.
- Check `e.origin` and `e.source` on iframe messages, and post to the exact hfy origin.
- Authorize tool calls in MCP servers from `_meta`, not from anything the model says.
- Run `hfy validate` after editing config.

Don't:
- Don't put tokens in URLs, cookies, localStorage or logs. Don't add URL parameters to `/embed`; they do nothing.
- Don't put secrets in grant `vars`: they reach the system prompt and every MCP server.
- Don't use one grant for two people. Each person in a room gets their own grant and actor.
- Don't build a document store inside hfy; expose knowledge as an MCP tool.
- Don't run one instance for several unrelated apps.

## Troubleshooting

- **Widget stays on "Connecting…"**: the host never answered `token-needed`. Check that the message listener runs, that the origin check uses the hfy origin, and that the grant endpoint returns `{token, expires_at}`.
- **iframe refuses to load (frame-ancestors)**: the host origin is missing from `server.cors_origins`.
- **401**: token expired, revoked or wrong instance. The widget asks for a new one automatically, so make sure the grant endpoint works for logged-in users.
- **403 on messages**: the grant's agent was removed from config. **403 on approvals**: only the turn's starter can decide.
- **400 on grant**: a required var is missing, or an undeclared var was sent.
- **The model never uses tools or asks in plain text**: the model is too small or lacks tool calling. Try a larger model, or name the tool in the system prompt.
- **400 "the agent cannot see images"**: set `settings.vision: true` on that agent (only for models that accept images).
- **Model ignores an image**: the provider cannot fetch its URL. Local model servers need a URL reachable from their host, so set `filesystem.public_url` accordingly.
- **Uploads fail with S3**: the bucket CORS must allow PUT from the embed origins; `region=` is required in the dsn.
- **Startup error naming a line**: an unknown or misspelled config key.

## Not supported (v1)

Images returned by MCP tools (they become a text placeholder), semantic `tool_search` (keyword today), structured output, provider failover, an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` facade, script-tag embedding, cookie auth, quotas.
